Quick triage results after initial trace:
- Observed repeated KV cache churn on hot shards. Eviction rate spikes align with p95 jumps.
- Scheduler backlog increased during long-tail sequences (v2.3 increases average decode steps by ~12%). Batching windows grew and we started hitting a tight kernel path that does not benefit from the quantized decoder.
- A subset of nodes is running an older NNPX kernel selection, others picked the new heuristic — we think heuristic variance + longer sequences caused suboptimal kernel selection and higher CPU completions -> 502s when worker threads were throttled.

Proposed immediate actions (can do in parallel):
1) Canary rollback on 10% of traffic to v2.2 (safe path).
2) Force kernel_profile: conservative_decode on impacted node pool to avoid the high-latency path.
3) Increase KV prefix TTL and enable opportunistic prefix warming for hot keys.
4) Add a temporary rate limiter on long sequence requests from the client to shape load while we stabilize.

I'll prepare the rollout commands and playbook. If Marissa approves, Ops (David) can schedule the canary now.

—Jonas

Subject: Executive summary and proposed remediation / credit request — CloverCare incident (2027-07-20)

Executive summary (short):
- Impact: CloverCare private deployment experienced sustained p95 latency increase (~220ms -> ~1.2s) and ~45% throughput loss between 06:30–08:20 PT after v2.3 model rollout. This triggered elevated 502s and client-visible errors.
- Root cause (current view): Larger decode lengths for v2.3 combined with heterogeneous kernel selection heuristics caused KV churn and scheduler backlog; this pushed some nodes onto a higher-latency decode path and increased CPU completions leading to transient 502s.
- Actions taken: 10% canary rollback to v2.2 at 11:30 PT; forced conservative kernel_profile on impacted pool; increased KV prefix TTL and enabled prefix warming. Real-time metrics show p95 returning toward baseline within 12 minutes of canary start.
- Customer ask: SLA credit for the degradation window and a written mitigation plan.

Ask for Execs: approve a proactive credit (1 months of hosting credit amortized) to settle quickly — this reduces churn risk and is consistent with our customer-first SLA policy. If approved, I'll coordinate contracting and public statement with Legal & Finance.

Next steps (owners):
- Jonas: finalize permanent kernel heuristic fix and deploy across pool (ETA 72h).
- David: complete post-mortem with customer and provide node-level timeline (ETA 24h).
- Marissa: handle credit approval and exec comms.

I'll set a short 30-minute huddle at 09:00 PT tomorrow for final sign-off.

—Marissa
